description: Motif: a compact, classic Art Deco magnifying glass shaped exactly like a hand lens — one round lens with a single straight handle extending directly downward from the bottom of its rim, ending in a small stepped finial, the whole object no taller overall than about twice the lens's own diameter so it reads as one small emblem like a coin's mint mark. A tiny faceted starburst sparkle sits just to the side of the handle. The surrounding brass field is a deep warm amber gold, richly toned like the other struck medals in this same series, with a strong circular brushed sheen and pronounced dark shadow pooling around the lens rim and handle where the relief is deepest — a well-worn antique coin finish, not a pale or flat gold. Enamel accent: the glass of the lens only, a pale translucent blue enamel inlay with a soft highlight.

Motif: a round wicker basket brimming with flea-market finds struck in raised relief — the neck of a bottle, the corner of a small picture frame, a round trinket. Enamel accent: a soft piece of cloth draped over the basket rim, a muted green enamel inlay.

Motif: a wooden crate with its lid ajar, bric-a-brac emerging from the opening — a candlestick, a stack of books — with two or three tiny puffs of dust struck in low relief above. Enamel accent: the neck of one glass bottle sticking out of the crate, a deep bottle-green enamel inlay.

Motif: a showman's top hat resting at a jaunty angle on a crossed walking cane, with three small four-pointed Art Deco sparkles around it. Enamel accent: the hat's ribbon band, a burgundy enamel inlay.

Motif: a pair of small stylized Art Deco lips from which flows a long undulating speech ribbon, a smooth banner waving in two gentle S-curves across the medal. Enamel accent: the thin trim line along the ribbon's edge, a burgundy enamel inlay.

Motif: a town crier's brass speaking-trumpet, drawn as one bold solid cone — a narrow cylindrical mouthpiece that flares smoothly and dramatically into a wide, deep, funnel-shaped bell with a thick rounded rim, tilted upward at 30 degrees, its solid cone silhouette immediately readable as a horn on its own. A short distance beyond the bell's rim, clearly separated from it by a gap of plain flat brass, sits a small Art Deco sunburst of three or four short, thin, straight sound-ray lines, each no longer than half the bell rim's width, fanning outward like a compact hallmark stamp next to the horn rather than merging with it. Enamel accent: the cylindrical wooden handle grip below the mouthpiece, a warm red-brown enamel inlay; the horn itself stays bare brass.
